body:
Yes, the new console commands (and UX) is still unfinished and needs some testing before we should release it. The core components are there and seem to be solid. The UI/UX can benefit from some love though 😄 

That said, I think it could be a major feature for 3.0 - if we find the time do to the required work.
Maybe we can also start putting together a changelog for 3.0, and then decide if & what makes it into the release.

We have 900 commits on master since 2.0, so I think featurewise we're more than packed for 3.0 (options, contentviews, mitmweb, ...). 

I am really looking forward to have commands in mitmproxy, as it's going to be a fantastic feature. I just think that fixing the command ux will take a bit really, and we're far behind the 2-month schedule we agreed on at some point. There's really nothing that stops us from finishing commands immediately after 3.0 is out and ship 4.0 as soon as it's finished.

- always refresh UI after flow is finished (refs #2616)
 - count currently active replay
 - make replay thread daemonic so that users can exit mitmproxy
   if replay hangs. This is not perfect yet, but vastly better
   than how it has been.

body:
Thanks for the detailed feedback list, Max - it's very useful. Hiding commands for 3.0 is not an option - it's the core interaction paradigm now, so we must push on. Luckily, many of the issues you list are easily fixed and go away once we've taken the immediate next steps in the roadmap, added documentation, and so forth. So, much of this is just due to the fact that I had to step back from things in mid-flight, so to speak, which is unfortunate. 

Some notes:

- Path will be more obvious once we have fixed #2198, which will let us show "path" in the help prompts.
- A few of these are due to the fact that you don't know what the cuts mechanism does - which is not surprising because it's not documented. This will be fixed soon. 
- A few of the comments for the command list shows that you're interpreting this differently from the way I intended. This is meant to be a command palette, with documentation for all commands, including internal commands. It's the documentation and the playground from which people can hopefully assemble their own complex commands and key bindings. From that perspective, it doesn't make sense to say that `console.command` is not too useful in the list, or that `console.choose` is only useful internally, or that you would just press q/Q rather than select the quit command from the command palette. Also, executing a command that only works while viewing a flow while in the command list is expected to fail, though I do see why you'd expect it to work if you've just come from a flow view. 
- Many of these issues here might be fixed if we have a help string for each keyboard shortcut, which is displayed if a user prompt results. I don't want to hide the underlying commands entirely, though, because we do want people to be able to inspect them and grow to use them directly. Ultimately, I would like the command prompt to grow much more powerful, with completion for arguments like paths, and with an "underlay" to show what the expected arguments for the current command is. 

I'm going to edit your list to add issues for items that translate into obvious actions, and to trim items that don't make sense to me. Let's keep the list up to date as we move to 3.0.

- [ ] "shift tab" to focus on the next pane doesn't work for me.
  - [ ] "Key bindings" up/down navigation is broken, down is interpreted as page down if I was scrolling up before.

Both of these work for me, so if you could open an issue with some more info on how I can reproduce those, that would be excellent.

- [x] Pressing `r` shows `[cplayback:1]` for some reason. (#2621)

This is expected - pressing "r" adds one flow (the current focus) to the client replay buffer. The `[cplayback:N]` indicator shows the length of the client playback buffer. Once the buffer is empty, the playback buffer indicator goes away. You can add an arbitrary number of flows to the replay buffer with a flow specification to the `replay.client` command.

- [ ] `console.grideditor.{add,delete,editor,insert,readfilereadfile_escaped}`: "Not in a grideditor" even though I'm in a grideditor. Bug?

While you're viewing the command palette, you're not in a grid editor. Try typing these commands (or binding them to a key), and using them in one of the grid editors (e.g. editing cookies). Works for me.

- [ ] `console.flowview.mode` "Not viewing a flow", even though I was in the flow view before pressing Shift+C.

This is the command palette thing again. Works for me while viewing a flow.

- [ ] `console.flowview.mode.set` Shouldn't this take an argument? Also "Not viewing a flow".

Works while viewing a flow. The name here is clumsy, though - it pops up a prompt to allow the user to select the flow view mode. This could be renamed to `console.flowview.mode.prompt` and a corresponding `.set` command can be added that takes an argument.

- [ ] `console.edit.focus`: Needs docs and an example - not sure what it does at the moment. Doesn't modify the query of the currently focused flow.  
- [ ] `console.edit.focus.options  ->` Needs docs and an example - not sure what it does at the moment. "Command returned too much data for display".

Both of these work as expected - the bug is that they need proper docstrings. The `console.edit.focus` command starts editing a component of the current focus. The `console.edit.focus.options` returns the list of valid options that can be passed to `console.edit.focus`, and is intended to be used in scripts to prompt the user. You can see this in action in the default key binding for "e", which first prompts the user, then executes the command with the user's choice:

        console.choose.cmd Part console.edit.focus.options
        console.edit.focus {choice}

The "too much data" thing is worth thinking about. Some commands that have output that should be consumed programmatically return a lot of data, and we don't necessarily just want to dump it in the console. We can probably do better than the current message, though.
Everything here has either been addressed, or has a separate open ticket. Closing this to clear the milestone.
